settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: How agnts connects to your tools and how it behaves during runs.
settings.appearanceSub: Saved in this browser, applied right away
settings.themeHelp: System follows your device's day or night setting
settings.integrationsSub: Where tickets come from and where code is pushed
settings.claudeSub: The engine that does the coding
settings.modelsHelp: Pick which model runs each step. Haiku uses the least of your plan, Opus the most.
settings.moduleTabsHelp: Every stage runs on the module you pick, with its own models. Only the modules an Admin enabled for you are listed.
settings.modulesMixed: Stages use several modules now. Picking a module moves them all to it, at the same level (Opus becomes Muse Wonder).
settings.modelsHelpCodex: Pick which Codex model runs each step: name any model your OpenAI key can use.
settings.stageReviewHelpCodex: Reviews each result while you review it. Auto uses your default module's stronger model for complex tickets and its lighter one for the rest.
settings.codexModelNeeded: Name a Codex model for every step.
settings.stageAnalyze: Reading the ticket and asking questions
settings.stageCodingHelp: The main run. Uses most of your plan.
settings.stageRetryHelp: After failed tests, your feedback or a stopped run.
settings.stageHelperHelp: Small tasks like the idle usage refresh.
settings.stageLearnHelp: Reads each pushed change and writes lessons about what is new to the repository.
settings.stageChatHelp: Answers in the assistant chat, and spoken questions. Never runs on credits: it needs a connected account.
settings.stageDocumentsHelp: Writes documents and the notes and action items of a meeting.
settings.meetingAudioMuse: Meeting audio is always heard by Muse, the only module that hears audio; the notes are written by the model above.
settings.stageReviewHelp: Reviews each result while you review it. Auto uses Opus for complex tickets and Sonnet for the rest.
settings.maxTurnsHelp: The run stops and reports when it reaches this
settings.runBudgetHelp: The most one run on credits may spend; Muse is told to wrap up at 80% and stopped before going over
settings.allowHelp: Claude Code can run these without asking
settings.denyHelp: Always refused, even if a ticket asks for them. Pushing is done by agnts, never by Claude Code.
settings.commitsSub: Who commits appear from, and how pull requests open
settings.authorNameHelp: Leave empty to commit as each ticket's owner, with the name and email of their account
settings.authorEmailHelp: Must match your GitHub account to show as yours
settings.coAuthorHelp: Teammates can see which commits agnts wrote
settings.prTitleHelp: Placeholders {number}, {key}, {type}, {scope}, {subject} and {title}, as in the commit message format. A repository's or group's own format replaces it.
settings.runsSub: Defaults for every ticket and task
settings.askFirstHelp: Default for new Jira tickets. Tasks choose this when you create them.
settings.autoResume: Resume paused runs after the limit resets
settings.switchModules: Switch modules when one cannot run
settings.switchModulesHelp: When a module's account is at its limit, missing, or not enabled for the person, the run uses their next module at the same level (opus becomes Muse Wonder). Off: it waits for the module.
settings.autoLearnHelp: After a push, agnts looks for techniques the repository never used before and writes lessons under Learn. Uses plan usage only when no ticket is waiting.
settings.autoReviewHelp: While a change or report waits for you, agnts reviews it and shows its findings next to it. It never blocks approval.
settings.pauseAboveHelp: Session usage. Runs already going keep going.
settings.parallelHelp: More runs finish sooner but use your plan limit faster
settings.notifySub: Push to your phone and Telegram messages
settings.pushHelp: To the agnts app on your phone
settings.telegramHelp: Only sent once Telegram is connected on the Integrations page
settings.needsYouHelp: Questions to answer or changes to review
settings.stopped: When a run stops or pauses
settings.progress: When an agent finishes a step
settings.progressHelp: Analysis done, code written. Phone only, silent, one notification per ticket
settings.lessons: When agnts finds something new to learn
settings.secretsHelp: Tokens for Jira, GitHub and {agent} are stored encrypted on your server. This page never shows them.
settings.parallelSlots: {n, plural, one {# run} other {# runs}} at once
settings.parallelSlotsHelp: The workspace's slots. Change them in Workspace → Billing.
settings.claudeMoved: Claude is connected per workspace now.
settings.selfReviewHelp: When agnts's own code review finds a blocker or major problem, agnts sends it back to the coder once before you review. Needs the code review above.
settings.autoBriefHelp: Write a repository brief (architecture, recipes, conventions) when a repository's first ticket is analysed, and update it after every 10 merges. A brief reaches the agent only after you approve it.
settings.reflectHelp: When you ask for changes or reject work with a reason, agnts looks for a convention behind it and suggests a rule on the Rules page. Nothing applies until you adopt it.
settings.ciRed: When a watched branch goes red
settings.modelsHelpMuse: Pick which model runs each step. Muse Spark costs the least; Muse Wonder is stronger and costs more.
settings.stageCodingHelpMuse: The main run. Spends the most.
settings.stageReviewHelpMuse: Reviews each result while you review it. Auto uses Muse Wonder for complex tickets and Muse Spark for the rest.
settings.allowHelpMuse: Muse Code can run these without asking
settings.denyHelpMuse: Always refused, even if a ticket asks for them. Pushing is done by agnts, never by Muse Code.
